STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits in a white bowl with a curved inner wall visible around the rim and the food surface is well below the rim, so this is a deep bowl (salad bowl).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a salad bowl is typically 20-25 cm wide.
b) Reference: the spinach leaves and chicken pieces are roughly 2-4 cm each, and the bowl spans about 5-6 times a chicken chunk of ~3 cm across the visible width, which suggests roughly 20-22 cm. The bowl fills most of the frame width, consistent with a medium salad bowl.
Reconciled width: about 22 cm.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Vessel capacity: 0.35 x 22^3 / 1000 = 0.35 x 10.65 = 3.7 L (deep bowl).
- Fill: the food mound sits below the rim, peaking near about 0.6 of the depth, so fill ≈ 0.6; food volume = 3.7 x 0.6 x 0.6 ≈ 1.3 L = 1300 ml.
- Visible composition by area: chicken ~40%, cheese shavings ~15%, black beans ~10%, spinach ~25%, carrot ~5%, dressing/other ~5%.
- Chicken: 40% of 1300 ml = 520 ml x 1.0 = 520 g? This over-weights a loose mound, so I apply the mound average (about half the peak, already included in the fill); using the bowl split with spinach as the bulk: chicken ≈ 150 g.
- Spinach (raw leafy greens, 0.15 g/ml): 25% of 1300 = 325 ml x 0.15 ≈ 50 g.
- Black beans (chopped/cooked legumes, ~0.8 g/ml): ~10% of 1300 = 130 ml x 0.8 ≈ 100 g. Counting visible beans (~20 visible, ~20 hidden) at ~1 g each would give far less, so use the volume estimate, trimmed to ~60 g.
- Cheese (shaved, 1.0 g/ml): ~15% = 195 ml x 1.0 ≈ 60 g, trimmed to ~40 g as shavings are light.
- Carrot (0.6 g/ml): ~5% = 65 ml x 0.6 ≈ 40 g.
- Dressing: a light smear, ~15 g.

Total ≈ 150 + 50 + 60 + 40 + 40 + 15 ≈ 355 g.
